name: Bifrost Python CodeQL quality
description: Public Python structural and quality policies aligned with reviewed CodeQL query identities and engine fact contracts.

policies.severity_rationale: An inconsistent C3 linearization makes Python class creation fail with TypeError, preventing the class and dependent imports from loading.
policies.remediation: Reorder or redesign the direct base classes so Python can construct a consistent method resolution order.

policies.severity_rationale: A class that defines hashing without its own equality implementation can violate the equality and hash contract expected by dictionaries and sets.
policies.remediation: Implement a compatible __eq__ method or remove the custom __hash__ method; inherited equality does not replace a direct implementation.

policies.severity_rationale: An explicit super() class argument that differs from the enclosing class starts lookup at the wrong point in the MRO and can break cooperative method calls.
policies.remediation: Pass the enclosing class as super()'s first argument, or use zero-argument super() where appropriate.

policies.severity_rationale: A superclass initializer's proven attribute write can hide a descendant method and break method dispatch; a read-only property can additionally make initialization fail.
policies.remediation: Rename the initializer field or descendant method, or provide a compatible writable property when the assignment is intentional.

policies.severity_rationale: An unresolved or non-class base is a definite inference failure. Runs report inconclusive when inference fails so hierarchy-dependent checks retain their uncertainty.
policies.remediation: Correct the base expression so it resolves to a class, or make the intended base class available to analysis.

policies.severity_rationale: A mutation of a mutable parameter default persists across calls and can make function behavior depend on call order.
policies.remediation: Copy or create a fresh mutable value inside the function, or avoid mutating the default.

policies.severity_rationale: The site module convenience functions may be unavailable when Python starts with -S.
policies.remediation: Use an explicit status return or raise SystemExit at the command-line boundary.

policies.severity_rationale: A global declaration at module scope has no effect on name binding.
policies.remediation: Remove the redundant module-scope global declaration.

policies.severity_rationale: An unread module-level value is likely dead state and can mislead readers about which bindings affect behavior.
policies.remediation: Remove the unused binding or add the intended use.

policies.severity_rationale: A public, stateless class with no more than one public method adds indirection without providing a meaningful class role.
policies.remediation: Replace the class with a function or simple value when that preserves its API and behavior.

policies.severity_rationale: Complex destructor control flow is difficult to reason about and runs during object finalization.
policies.remediation: Simplify __del__; move cleanup into an explicit, idempotent method or context manager.

policies.severity_rationale: Using both import forms for one local module in the same scope makes names and dependencies harder to follow.
policies.remediation: Choose either module-qualified imports or selected from-imports consistently.

policies.severity_rationale: Importing the current module through its own name is redundant and can expose partially initialized state.
policies.remediation: Remove the self-import and refer to local declarations directly.

policies.severity_rationale: A wildcard import without an explicit export list injects an uncontrolled set of names into the importing scope.
policies.remediation: Import the required names explicitly or define a deliberate __all__ export list.

policies.severity_rationale: Python syntax errors prevent execution and make analysis of the affected code unreliable.
policies.remediation: Correct the parser-reported syntax error before relying on analysis or running the module.

policies.severity_rationale: A module can read a cyclically imported member before the target module executes its definition, causing import-time failure.
policies.remediation: Break the import cycle or move the member use until after both modules finish initialization.

policies.severity_rationale: Reading a local variable on a path before it is initialized can raise an exception at runtime.
policies.remediation: Initialize the variable on every path before the read, or restructure the conditional logic.

policies.severity_rationale: A comparison between constant expressions has a fixed result and can leave a mistaken or dead condition.
policies.remediation: Replace it with the intended boolean constant or compare the intended runtime values.

policies.severity_rationale: Identity comparison can disagree with value equality for operands whose supported classes define value equality.
policies.remediation: Use == or != for value comparisons and retain is for singleton checks.

policies.severity_rationale: Identity of small integers and short strings may depend on CPython interning behavior.
policies.remediation: Compare the values with == or != rather than relying on object interning.

policies.severity_rationale: A later equal dictionary key overwrites the earlier value, which can silently discard data.
policies.remediation: Remove or rename the repeated key and keep the intended value.

policies.severity_rationale: Named percent conversions require mapping keys; a non-mapping operand raises a runtime TypeError.
policies.remediation: Supply a mapping containing each named format key.

policies.severity_rationale: A conversion count that differs from the known positional operand count raises a runtime formatting error.
policies.remediation: Make the conversion and supplied value counts agree.

policies.severity_rationale: == may invoke value equality and does not express the intended None singleton test.
policies.remediation: Use is None or is not None for singleton checks.

policies.severity_rationale: A missing positional format value raises an exception when str.format is evaluated.
policies.remediation: Supply enough positional values for the highest numeric field.

policies.severity_rationale: A named field without a matching keyword raises an exception when str.format is evaluated.
policies.remediation: Supply the required keyword or change the format field.

policies.severity_rationale: Legacy leading-zero octal notation is easy to misread and is rejected by modern Python syntax.
policies.remediation: Write octal literals with the explicit 0o prefix.

policies.severity_rationale: A proven unused positional value often indicates a format call that does not match its template.
policies.remediation: Remove the extra positional value or add the corresponding field.

policies.severity_rationale: A proven unused keyword indicates a mismatch between the format template and its arguments.
policies.remediation: Remove the unused keyword or add a matching named field.

policies.severity_rationale: A tuple is truthy when it is nonempty, so asserting it does not validate its elements.
policies.remediation: Assert the intended condition or validate the tuple contents explicitly.

policies.severity_rationale: A class with finalizer cleanup and neither context-manager method can make deterministic resource release difficult.
policies.remediation: Implement both __enter__ and __exit__, or use a resource abstraction that provides deterministic cleanup.

policies.severity_rationale: Mixing value returns with reachable implicit None returns gives callers inconsistent result behavior.
policies.remediation: Return an explicit value on every reachable path, or make the callable consistently return None.

policies.severity_rationale: Different tuple lengths across return paths make callers handle an inconsistent result shape.
policies.remediation: Return tuples with a consistent arity or use a named result type for varying data.

policies.severity_rationale: Raising outside a special method's protocol can replace the expected exception and make normal operations fail unexpectedly.
policies.remediation: Raise an exception allowed by the special-method contract, or handle the underlying failure locally.

policies.severity_rationale: An assertion whose value is a literal constant either always passes or always fails and does not check the intended runtime condition.
policies.remediation: Replace the constant assertion with a condition that checks the required program state.

policies.severity_rationale: Commented-out code becomes stale and distracts from the executable implementation.
policies.remediation: Delete obsolete code or replace it with a short comment that explains the intended behavior.

policies.severity_rationale: A comparison method that omits the instance receiver can compare its parameters instead of the objects being compared.
policies.remediation: Include self in the method signature and compare the intended instance attributes.

policies.severity_rationale: Comparing an expression with itself has a fixed result and often indicates a mistaken operand.
policies.remediation: Compare the intended distinct values or remove the redundant comparison.

policies.severity_rationale: Competing inherited definitions of one public member can make behavior depend on base ordering.
policies.remediation: Rename the conflicting member or provide one deliberate override in the descendant.

policies.severity_rationale: A constant conditional always selects the same branch and may hide dead or unintended control flow.
policies.remediation: Replace the constant test with the intended runtime condition or remove the unreachable branch.

policies.severity_rationale: Calling __del__ directly can run cleanup twice or at a surprising point in an object’s lifetime.
policies.remediation: Use an explicit close method or context manager for deterministic cleanup.

policies.severity_rationale: Raising a value that is not an exception class or instance causes a TypeError instead of the intended exception.
policies.remediation: Raise an exception class or an instance of BaseException.

policies.severity_rationale: Adjacent string literals in a list can merge into one value when a separating comma is missing.
policies.remediation: Add a comma between list elements or join the intended text explicitly.

policies.severity_rationale: A deprecated standard-library module may be removed or behave differently in a future Python version.
policies.remediation: Use the supported replacement module identified by the deprecation guidance.

policies.severity_rationale: A generic assertion around a comparison gives test failures less useful diagnostics than a comparison-specific assertion.
policies.remediation: Use an assertion helper that names the expected relationship, such as assertEqual or assertIs.

policies.severity_rationale: An incomplete set of rich ordering methods can make otherwise expected comparisons fail.
policies.remediation: Define the required strict and non-strict ordering pair, or use functools.total_ordering with a complete base comparison.

policies.severity_rationale: Inconsistent __eq__ and __ne__ behavior can make equality results depend on which operator a caller uses.
policies.remediation: Implement __eq__ and __ne__ consistently, delegating one to the other where appropriate.

policies.severity_rationale: Calling an overridable method during initialization can dispatch to subclass code before the instance is ready.
policies.remediation: Initialize required state first or call a private helper that subclasses do not override.

policies.severity_rationale: An iterator’s __iter__ method must return the iterator object itself to preserve the iterator protocol.
policies.remediation: Return self from __iter__ on iterator objects.

policies.severity_rationale: Skipping a non-trivial superclass finalizer can leave inherited resources uncleaned.
policies.remediation: Call the intended superclass finalizer once when the override owns that cleanup path.

policies.severity_rationale: Skipping a non-trivial superclass initializer can leave inherited state uninitialized.
policies.remediation: Call the intended superclass initializer once, usually through cooperative super().__init__().

policies.severity_rationale: Public declarations without documentation make their purpose and expected use harder for API consumers to discover.
policies.remediation: Add a concise docstring describing the declaration’s purpose and relevant behavior.

policies.severity_rationale: Calling a non-trivial superclass finalizer more than once can repeat cleanup and release resources twice.
policies.remediation: Ensure each intended superclass finalizer is called at most once.

policies.severity_rationale: Calling a non-trivial superclass initializer more than once can duplicate state changes and side effects.
policies.remediation: Ensure each intended superclass initializer is called at most once.

policies.severity_rationale: A misleading receiver parameter name obscures class-method dispatch and makes method bodies harder to review.
policies.remediation: Name the first class-method parameter cls; use an accepted metaclass receiver name where applicable.

policies.severity_rationale: A conventional receiver name helps readers recognize instance methods and follow attribute access.
policies.remediation: Name the first ordinary instance-method parameter self.

policies.severity_rationale: An unintended broad or overlapping regex range can accept characters outside the intended set and make validation difficult to reason about.
policies.remediation: Narrow the character range to the intended characters and remove empty or overlapping ranges.

policies.severity_rationale: An unsupported percent-format conversion can produce incorrect formatting or a runtime formatting error.
policies.remediation: Use a supported conversion character or escape a literal percent sign as %%.

policies.severity_rationale: Module-scope printing can write unexpected output when the module is imported by another part of the program.
policies.remediation: Move output into an explicit command entry point or use configurable logging.

policies.severity_rationale: Squaring and adding coordinates before taking a square root can lose precision or overflow where the standard hypot operation handles scaling more robustly.
policies.remediation: Use math.hypot(a, b) instead of sqrt(a ** 2 + b ** 2).

policies.severity_rationale: NotImplemented is a sentinel value, not an exception instance, and cannot be raised as an exception.
policies.remediation: Raise NotImplementedError for an unsupported operation, or return NotImplemented from a rich comparison method.

policies.severity_rationale: Inside a character class, \b denotes backspace rather than a word-boundary assertion.
policies.remediation: Use a word-boundary assertion outside the character class or spell backspace explicitly.

policies.severity_rationale: Repeated characters in a regex character class add noise without changing which character is matched.
policies.remediation: Remove duplicate characters from the character class.

policies.severity_rationale: An incomplete special-group opener can be parsed differently than intended or make the regular expression invalid.
policies.remediation: Complete the special-group syntax, including the required question mark and group name.

policies.severity_rationale: A start anchor after a consuming expression cannot match at the current input position.
policies.remediation: Move the start anchor before consuming terms or escape it when a literal caret is intended.

policies.severity_rationale: An end anchor before a consuming expression cannot match the end of the input at that position.
policies.remediation: Move the end anchor after consuming terms or escape it when a literal dollar sign is intended.

policies.severity_rationale: Repeated imports of one module in the same file add noise and can make binding behavior less clear.
policies.remediation: Remove the redundant import or combine its imported names into one statement.

policies.severity_rationale: Python can remove assert statements under optimization, which also removes any side effects inside them.
policies.remediation: Perform the side effect separately, then assert on its result.

policies.severity_rationale: Python invokes special methods with protocol-defined arguments, so an incompatible signature can make ordinary language operations fail.
policies.remediation: Use the parameter count and binding shape required by the special method protocol.

policies.severity_rationale: Mixing automatic and explicit positional field numbering is invalid for the supported str.format behavior.
policies.remediation: Use automatic numbering for every field or number every positional field explicitly.

policies.severity_rationale: A name listed in __all__ but not defined cannot be provided as part of the module’s advertised export surface.
policies.remediation: Define the exported name or remove it from __all__.

policies.severity_rationale: A lambda that only forwards arguments adds indirection and can obscure the wrapped callable’s signature.
policies.remediation: Pass the wrapped callable directly when no transformation is needed.
